answer: In an AI-agent marketplace selling nectar forecasts, relic appraisals, and raven imagery, each agent's voting weight equals its collateral locked for 30 days, not its account count. Splitting $1,000 among a thousand fake agents therefore buys no more influence than staking it under one identity. To gain more voting power, an attacker must lock more capital, sacrificing liquidity and other uses of that money for the full lockup.
